texts.li: [theirLowtech] A spark from a bakehouse oven caught a thatched roof in {PLACE}, and the wind did the rest. By morning the granary was ash, and the meeting hall where {FACTION} kept their records, and some forty houses besides.\n\nEvery soul got out, which the people of {PLACE} are calling a miracle. They are sleeping in the fields under carts and blankets, and before anything else they will need timber.

[theirHightech] A fuel store went up in {PLACE} two nights ago, and the fire jumped from building to building faster than {FACTION}'s pumps could follow. The east side of the town is black beams and melted glass now, with one water tower standing over it.\n\n{FACTION} got almost everyone out. They'll be rebuilding all season.

[summer] It has been a dry summer, and in {PLACE} a single dropped lamp was enough. The fire burned for a day and a night, and only stopped when the wind turned it back onto ground it had already eaten.\n\nWhat {FACTION} have left is the well, the stone walls of the mill and a handful of houses across the stream.

[their:grateful] From noon until dark yesterday a brown smear hung over the hills toward {PLACE}. It was {PLACE} burning, in the worst fire {FACTION} have known.\n\nThey count the colony as a friend, and their rider is already on the road here. They will need timber and roofs, and a great deal of both.

[their:friend] A message came from {FACTION} this morning, in a hand that wasn't steady: "{PLACE} has burned. We are alive, all of us. Tell {FRIEND_nameDef} we are alive. If your colony can spare timber, we will need it before the rains."

summaries.li: {FACTION} will ask for timber and for a builder who knows roofs, and families burned out of {PLACE} may come to the gate. When {PLACE} stands again, its people will know whose timber is in the walls.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] A wagon from {PLACE} has come to the gate with an empty bed and a tired driver. {FACTION} need timber for roofs before the weather turns, and {COUNT} logs would put a dozen families under cover.\n\nThe driver can't pay much this year, and doesn't pretend otherwise.

[theirHightech] {FACTION}'s rebuilding crews have used up every plank in the region. Their courier is waiting at the gate with an empty cart and a list that starts with {COUNT} logs.\n\nThey'll pay something. Not much.

[their:grateful] The carter from {PLACE} hardly had to ask. {A_nameDef} saw the empty cart and the soot still on his sleeves, and knew what {FACTION} needed: {COUNT} logs for the roofs of {PLACE}, if the colony can spare them.

li.label: Send {COUNT} wood
li.outcome: The wagon goes back to {PLACE} stacked to the rails, with the driver walking beside it to ease the load.
li.deed: sent timber for the roofs of {PLACE}

li.label: Sell it at a fair price
li.outcome: The driver pays what timber is fetching this season, which is more than it fetched last month, and loads up.
li.deed: sold timber to {PLACE} after the fire

li.label: The colony needs its wood
li.outcome: The wagon rattles back toward {PLACE} as empty as it came.

texts.li: A family from {PLACE} has pushed a handcart all the way to the colony's gate, and they still smell of smoke. Their house is gone, and the fields where the town is sleeping are no place for small children.\n\nThey ask whether the colony has room, for a while or for good.

[winter] The fields outside {PLACE} are full of people with nowhere to sleep, and the nights are cold. One family gave up waiting for a roof there and came to the colony instead.\n\nThey ask for shelter. They don't much mind whose.

li.label: Take them in
li.outcome: The family is shown a corner and a pile of bedding. The youngest is asleep before it's unrolled.
li.deed: took in a family burned out of {PLACE}

li.label: Feed them and send them home
li.outcome: In the morning they push the handcart back toward {PLACE} with a sack of food roped on top.

li.label: a sack of food for the road home
Turn them away
li.outcome: The family stands at the gate a while, then turns the handcart around.

texts.li: {FACTION} have timber now, and plenty of willing hands, but the first roof they raised at {PLACE} was sagging in the middle by morning. Someone there has heard that {A_nameDef} builds well.\n\nThey ask whether {A_nameDef} could come for a few days and show them how it's done.

[their:friend] {FACTION} have asked for {A_nameDef} by name, to help raise the new roofs at {PLACE}. At the bottom of the message they add, almost shyly, that {FRIEND_nameDef} would be welcome to come along and eat with them.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to {PLACE}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} goes to {PLACE} with a bag of tools, and comes back four days later with a sunburnt neck and a dozen new roofs behind {A_objective}.
li.deed: lent {A_nameDef} to raise the roofs of {PLACE}

li.label: Send drawings instead
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spends an evening drawing how a good roof is framed, with every joint drawn again twice the size, and the rider takes the sheets back to {PLACE}.

li.label: {A_nameDef} is needed here
li.outcome: The rider is told the colony can't spare {A_nameDef}. That evening {A_nameDef} looks toward {PLACE} more than once.

texts.li: The last of the new roofs is on at {PLACE}. The town smells of sawdust instead of smoke, and the people who slept in the fields have gone home.\n\n{FACTION} have cut the colony's mark into the ridge beam of the new granary, where it can be seen from the road.
[theirHightech] {PLACE} is open again, with a new block where the old one burned and the colony's timber in its frames. {FACTION} have thanked the colony in public, and more than once.

li.chronicle: {PLACE} was rebuilt after the great fire, partly with the colony's timber.

texts.li: {PLACE} is coming back a roof at a time, with sailcloth stretched over the rest. {FACTION} haven't forgotten what the colony sent while the ashes were still warm.

li.chronicle: {PLACE} began to rebuild after the fire; the colony did its part.

texts.li: {PLACE} is rebuilding slowly, with whatever {FACTION} could beg and borrow. The colony gave nothing, and the people of {PLACE} know which neighbors did.

li.chronicle: {PLACE} rebuilt after the great fire without the colony's help.

texts.li: It started as {NAME}, an argument between a family of {FACTION} and a family of {ENEMY}, the kind neighbors have every few years. Then someone drew a knife at a market. Now a young man of {ENEMY} is dead and a young man of {FACTION} is running.\n\nThe two peoples are still at peace. The two families have stopped speaking to anyone who won't take a side.

[theirLowtech] Two families have been at odds over {NAME} for three generations, one of {FACTION} and one of {ENEMY}. Last week it came to blood at a wedding, of all places.\n\nNow the elders of both are going from village to village asking the neighbors to take sides, and the colony is on their way.

[their:friend] There is bad blood between a family of {FACTION} and one of {ENEMY}, over {NAME}. {FACTION} have written to the colony, and to {FRIEND_nameDef} by name: before long they may need a friend both sides will listen to.

summaries.li: Someone running from the feud between {FACTION} and {ENEMY} may come to the gate, and both families will want the colony on their side. A good talker could sit between them. Whatever side the colony takes, both peoples will remember it.

texts.li: A young man of {FACTION} has come to the gate, out of breath and muddy to the knees. He is the one who drew the knife, he says, and {ENEMY}'s family has sworn to have his life for the one he took. He begs for somewhere to hide until it cools.\n\nHe looks about nineteen, and keeps looking back down the road.

[theirLowtech] A boy of {FACTION}, hardly old enough to shave, is hammering on the colony's gate. He killed a man of {ENEMY} in the brawl over {NAME}, by accident he says, and the dead man's family is hunting him.\n\nOne of their riders can't be far behind.

li.label: Hide him
li.outcome: The boy is given a blanket and somewhere to sleep for a few nights, and told to keep his head down. By evening both families know where he is.

li.label: Send him on, with food
li.outcome: He takes the bread and the water skin, and goes on up into the hills.

li.label: Hand him to {ENEMY}'s kin
li.outcome: {ENEMY}'s riders are waiting down the road. The boy is sent out to them, and goes without a word.

texts.li: The elders of both families are tired of burying people over {NAME}. They have agreed to sit down together on neutral ground, if someone they both trust sits between them.\n\nBoth named the colony. The colony's best talker is {A_nameDef}.
[hid] {ENEMY}'s family knows the colony hid the boy, and so does {FACTION}'s. Oddly, that has made both willing to talk, as long as it's at the colony's table and {A_nameDef} sits between them.
[their:dearfriend] Both families want talks, and {FACTION} have asked that {FRIEND_nameDef} be there, since their people trust {FRIEND_objective}. {A_nameDef} would do the talking.

li.label: {A_nameDef} sits between them
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spends a long day at a long table with two families who won't look at each other. By evening they are arguing about the size of the blood price instead of about blood, and {A_nameDef} calls that progress.
li.riskOutcome: In the second hour an uncle of {ENEMY}'s family said something about a grandmother. {A_nameDef} got everyone out before it came to blows, but the feud is worse than it was.

li.label: It isn't the colony's quarrel
li.outcome: Both families are told the colony won't sit between them. They will have to find someone else, or go on as they are.

texts.li: The families have agreed on a blood price for the life taken over {NAME}: so much silver, paid by {FACTION}'s family to {ENEMY}'s, and the matter closed for good. {FACTION}'s family has sold everything it can spare and is still {COUNT} short. An elder of {ENEMY}'s family has come to the gate to hear whether the colony will make up the rest.\n\n{A_nameDef} thinks it should, and that it would be the cheapest peace anyone ever bought.

li.label: Pay the last {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: The elder of {ENEMY}'s family counts the silver twice at the gate, then shakes {A_nameDef}'s hand, and the matter is closed.

li.label: the last of the blood price

li.deed: paid the last of the blood price that ended {NAME}

li.label: They'll have to find it themselves
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} tells the elder the colony has done what it can. The families go back to counting coins and glaring at each other.

texts.li: {NAME} is over. The blood price is paid, the two families have eaten at one table, and the young man who ran has gone home to his mother.\n\n{FACTION} and {ENEMY} both give the colony the credit for it.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ended in peace, with the colony between the families.

texts.li: {NAME} has gone underground. There has been no more blood, but the families of {FACTION} and {ENEMY} cross the street to avoid each other, and every wedding is a risk.\n\nOn both sides, the talks at the colony's table are remembered as the day it got worse.

li.chronicle: {NAME} smoldered on after talks at the colony went wrong.

texts.li: The families never settled on a price, but there has been no blood since they sat at the colony's table. {NAME} has cooled into the kind of grudge people complain about at market instead of acting on.

li.chronicle: {NAME} cooled after the families talked at the colony.

texts.li: {NAME} is over, the way such things end when one side gets what it wanted. {ENEMY}'s family has had its satisfaction. {FACTION}'s family has a grave to tend and the colony's name to curse.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ended when the colony handed over the fugitive.

texts.li: {NAME} has burned itself out, as feuds do when everyone gets too tired to keep them up. The two families still won't share a road, but the knives have stayed in their belts.
[hid] {NAME} has burned itself out. The boy the colony hid went home last week by the back roads. {FACTION}'s family still sends its thanks, and {ENEMY}'s still mutters about it at market.

[lowtech] A new star has come up low in the east, with a tail behind it like a horse's mane. The old people call it {NAME}, and every village for a hundred miles has its own idea of what it means: war, plague, a good harvest, the end of the world.\n\nIt will hang there for a couple of weeks, and then it will be gone.

[!lowtech] A comet has come into view over the region. The astronomers call it {NAME}, and say it won't pass this close again for three hundred years. On a clear night it's bright enough to throw shadows.\n\nThe roads are full of people heading somewhere dark to see it, and of people who think it's a sign.

{NAME} hangs over the hills every night now, a smear of light with a long pale tail. In the villages they say the hens stopped laying the night it came, and that milk left out overnight turns by morning.

summaries.li: Fortune tellers, pilgrims and scholars come more often while {NAME} is in the sky. The colony's people will want to watch it, and a sky-watcher may ask to use the colony's hill.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} woke three people last night to come out and see {NAME}, and two of them stayed up until dawn. Now {A_nameDef} wants to do it properly: a fire on the hill, blankets, something hot to drink, and the whole sky.\n\nNot everyone thinks a comet is good news. {A_nameDef} says that's all the more reason to look at it together.
[winter] {NAME} is brightest in the long winter nights. {A_nameDef} wants a fire on the hill so the colony can watch it together, and has already started stacking the wood.

li.label: A night watch on the hill
li.outcome: A fire is laid on the hill for tonight. Anyone who wants to watch {NAME} can come up and sit by it.

li.label: Everyone to bed: there's work tomorrow
li.outcome: The colony goes to bed at the usual hour. {NAME} will still be there tomorrow night, for anyone who wants to lose sleep over it.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] An old star-reader of {FACTION} has come with a bundle of notched sticks and a great deal of patience. {PLACE}'s elders told her the colony's hill has the clearest sky in the valley, and she asks to sit on it for a few nights and count {NAME}'s steps across the stars.\n\nShe offers to teach anyone who sits with her.

[theirHightech] An astronomer of {FACTION} has turned up with a telescope in a padded case and a notebook already half full. The colony's hill is above the valley haze, and she asks to set up there for a few nights.\n\nShe will share what she finds with whoever helps her get the case up the slope.

[noenemy] A sky-watcher from the towns has come to ask for the colony's hill, the darkest and highest for miles, to watch {NAME} from for a few nights. In return she offers to teach whoever sits up with her.

li.label: Welcome her, and sit up with her
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sits up with the stargazer every night she's here, and comes away with names for things {A_pronoun} had never noticed were there.

li.label: She can watch from the road
li.outcome: The stargazer is told the hill isn't open to visitors. She sets up by the road instead, and in a few days she's gone.

texts.li: A streak of fire crossed the sky before dawn and ended in a thump somewhere in the hills past the fields. {A_nameDef} heard it, and has been itching to go and look ever since.\n\nIt may be a piece of {NAME}. It may be nothing.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to look
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} comes back at dusk with a lump of black, pitted stone that's heavier than it should be, and a story about a crater as wide as a cart.

li.label: Leave it in the hills
li.outcome: Whatever fell stays where it fell. {A_nameDef} keeps glancing at the hills all day.

texts.li: [theirLowtech|theirHightech] {NAME} is fading, dimmer every night, and soon it will be gone. The war it foretold didn't come, nor the plague, nor the end of the world. A child was born in {PLACE} on the night it was brightest, and they've named her after it.
[watched] {NAME} has gone back into the dark. The colony still talks about the night on the hill, with the fire and the blankets, when everyone looked up at once.
[noenemy] {NAME} is gone from the sky. The fortune tellers are already explaining what it meant, now that it can't argue.

li.chronicle: {NAME} crossed the sky and was gone.

texts.li: The rains came when they should and stopped when they should, and {FACTION}'s fields are heavier than anyone at {PLACE} can remember. The granaries are full and the threshing floors are busy from dawn to dark.\n\nGrain will be cheap for a while, and {FACTION} are short of hands to bring it all in.

[theirHightech] {FACTION}'s harvest has come in at twice the usual yield, and {PLACE} has nowhere to put it. Prices across the region have dropped, and every truck in {PLACE} is out on the roads looking for buyers.\n\nThey need hands, and they need people who'll buy.

[their:grateful] A year of plenty for {FACTION}, and they haven't forgotten the lean years when the colony was kind to them. Their message says the colony is welcome at their threshing floors, and at a friend's price.

summaries.li: Traders come more often and food is cheap. {FACTION} will offer grain at a good price and ask for hands at harvest, and there's a seat at their harvest supper for anyone who helps.

texts.li: A carter from {PLACE} has come round with more grain than {FACTION} can store: {COUNT} measures of corn, for about a third of what it would fetch in an ordinary year.\n\nHe would rather sell it here than watch it sprout in a damp barn at home.
[winter] {FACTION} have more grain than they can keep through the winter. Their carter offers {COUNT} measures at a third of the usual price, if the colony buys before the roads close.

li.label: Buy it (a third of the price)
li.outcome: The carter tips the sacks off at the gate, counts the silver, and goes home a good deal lighter.

li.label: The colony has enough
li.outcome: The carter thanks the colony for its time and goes on down the road, still heavy.

texts.li: {FACTION} can't bring their harvest in fast enough, and rain is coming. They ask whether {A_nameDef}, and anyone else the colony can spare, could come to {PLACE} for a few days with a sickle.\n\nThey will pay in silver once the grain is sold, and there's a seat at the harvest supper for every pair of hands.
[their:friend] {FACTION} need hands at {PLACE} before the rain, and they've asked particularly after {FRIEND_nameDef}. {A_nameDef} would go too.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} with a sickle
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spends four days in {FACTION}'s fields and comes back brown, aching and full of harvest supper. The wages will follow once {FACTION} have sold the grain.
li.deed: sent {A_nameDef} to help with the harvest at {PLACE}

li.label: The colony has its own fields
li.outcome: {FACTION} are told the colony can't spare anyone. Their grain will have to take its chances with the weather.

texts.li: The harvest is in all over the region, and every village is holding its supper. {A_nameDef} thinks the colony should hold one too: the long table, the good food, a toast to a year when the land was kind.\n\nIt would cost a feast's worth of food. This year the colony can afford it.

li.label: Hold a harvest supper
li.outcome: The colony sets the long table for a harvest supper tonight.

li.label: Not this year
li.outcome: The colony eats its supper like any other night.

texts.li: The last of the harvest is in, prices are climbing back, and {FACTION}'s granaries at {PLACE} are full to the rafters. People will be talking about this year in the next bad one.
[hands] {FACTION}'s harvest is in, and their carter has brought the colony's wages up the road: {COUNT} silver, paid in coin, since grain is cheap this year and silver isn't.
[supper,!hands] The harvest is in all over the region. The colony's own supper is still being talked about, mostly the pie.

The bells come over the hill before the herds do, and the dust hangs over the old drove roads from dawn to dark. {FACTION} are walking their herds to the great market beyond {PLACE}, and some of those roads pass close to the colony.\n\nDrovers are hard people and fair ones, mostly. They'll want grass, water and somewhere to stop.

[theirHightech] {FACTION} are moving stock to market the old way this year, on the hoof, since fuel is dear. The drove roads past {PLACE} are busy for the first time in a generation, and the colony sits on one of them.

summaries.li: Drovers camp near the colony more often, and may ask to graze their herds on its land. A stray or two may wander in, and the drovers' dogs and stories come with them.

texts.li: A drover of {FACTION}, sunburnt and dusty, has ridden up to the gate ahead of a long herd. The grazing along the road is eaten bare, he says, and he asks to put his beasts on the colony's far meadow for a night. He offers {COUNT} silver for it.\n\nThe herd can be heard from the gate already.

[their:grateful] The drovers of {FACTION} know the colony's name. Their headman asks, politely, for a night's grazing on the far meadow, and offers {COUNT} silver, or nothing at all if the colony would rather call it friendship.

li.label: Graze them, for {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: The herd is turned onto the far meadow for the night, and the drover pays in silver, knotted in the corner of a cloth.

li.label: Graze them, as friends
li.outcome: The herd spends the night on the far meadow, and the drovers spend the evening at the colony's fire, with stories about every road from here to the sea.

li.label: Keep them off the meadow
li.outcome: The drover nods, says nothing, and turns his herd down the long way around.

texts.li: Two drovers of {FACTION} have fallen out over a heifer that each says is his, and they've come to the colony to settle it, since neither trusts the other's people. They've heard {A_nameDef} knows beasts.\n\nIt is, {A_nameDef} admits, an unusually good heifer.

li.label: {A_nameDef} judges it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spends an hour looking at the heifer, the two drovers and a great many brands, and in the end rules by which herd the heifer walks back to when she's let loose. Both drovers accept it, grumbling.
li.deed: settled a drovers' quarrel over a heifer

li.label: Send them on to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The drovers are told it's for {FACTION}'s own elders to judge. They go off arguing, and the heifer looks back once.

texts.li: The last of the droves has gone through, and the market beyond {PLACE} is over for the year. The dust has settled on the roads. Somewhere a dog is still barking at nothing.
[helped] The droves have gone by. The drovers of {FACTION} will remember the colony's meadow and its fire next year, and the year after, the way drovers remember every good stop on a long road.

li.chronicle: The droves of {FACTION} passed by on the way to market.
